title: Gravity & Friction
subtitle: One pulls everything down. The other decides whether it slides.
objectives: Describe gravity as a force between masses and distinguish mass from weight
Explain what friction is and what it depends on
Give cases where friction is wanted and cases where it is a problem

cards.title: Two forces decide almost everything you do
cards.text: Gravity never switches off. Friction decides whether you move, stop, grip or slide. Between them, most of daily physics.

cards.title: Every mass pulls every other mass
cards.text: It is not a property of Earth. It is a property of mass. Earth is just the biggest thing near you.
points: **More mass, more pull.** Further apart, less pull.
**Mass is how much stuff you are.** It does not change.
**Weight is the force** gravity puts on that mass. It does change.
**On the Moon** your mass is identical and your weight is about a sixth.

question.text: An astronaut on the Moon has…
options: the same mass and the same weight
the same mass and less weight
less mass and the same weight
question.explain: Mass is the amount of matter and never changes. Weight depends on the gravity you are standing in.

cards.title: Astronauts are falling, not weightless
cards.text: The station is only about 400 km up. Gravity there is still roughly ninety percent of what you feel now.
points: **They float** because they are falling around the Earth, not because gravity stopped.
**Free fall** means everything falls together, so nothing presses on anything.
**The right word** is microgravity, not zero gravity.
**Drop a ball on a falling lift** and it hangs there too.

cards.title: Surfaces are rough, even when they look smooth
cards.text: Friction is the force that resists sliding. It comes from the surfaces actually touching, down at a scale you cannot see.
points: **Rougher surfaces** generally grip more.
**Harder pressed together**, more friction.
**It always opposes** the direction you are trying to slide.
**It makes heat.** Rub your hands and feel where the energy went.

cards.title: Starting is harder than keeping going
cards.text: Push a heavy box. Nothing, nothing, nothing — then it suddenly gives and slides more easily.
points: **Static friction** holds something still. It is the larger one.
**Kinetic friction** acts once it is already sliding.
**That sudden give** is the moment static loses.
**Anti-lock brakes exist** for exactly this: a rolling tyre grips better than a skidding one.

question.text: Why is it harder to start a box moving than to keep it moving?
options: Static friction is greater than kinetic friction
question.explain: Static friction has to be overcome first. Once sliding, the smaller kinetic friction takes over.

cards.title: A car is a long argument about friction
cards.text: Some places you want every bit of it. Others you spend real money getting rid of it.
points: **Tyres and brakes** want maximum grip.
**Bearings and oil** want as little as possible.
**A skidding tyre** has swapped static grip for kinetic, and stops you slower.
**Wet road** puts a water film between rubber and tarmac, so grip falls.

cards.title: Fan bearings are a war on friction
cards.text: The shaft has to spin for thousands of hours. Everything around it is designed to let it.
points: **Bearings** keep metal from dragging on metal.
**Oil or grease** fills the gap so the surfaces barely touch.
**When it dries out**, friction returns as noise, heat and a slower blade.
**That rattle** is friction becoming audible.

question.text: Friction is always something engineers try to remove.
question.explain: Brakes, tyres, shoes and screws all depend on it. The skill is choosing where you want it.

terms.def: The attractive force between any two masses.
How much matter something contains. It does not change with location.
The force gravity exerts on a mass. It changes with location.
The force that resists one surface sliding over another.
Friction on something not yet moving. The larger of the two.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Gravity acts between masses. Mass stays, weight changes.
Astronauts float because they are falling, not because gravity stopped.
Static friction is bigger than kinetic. That is why starting is hard.
Friction is wanted in tyres and brakes, unwanted in bearings.

options: The amount of matter in an object
The force gravity exerts on a mass
quiz.explain: Mass is the matter. Weight is the force on it, so it changes with location.
quiz.objective: Describe gravity as a force between masses and distinguish mass from weight

quiz.text: Your mass on the Moon compared with on Earth is…
quiz.explain: Mass never changes with place. Only your weight is about a sixth.
quiz.objective: Describe gravity as a force between masses and distinguish mass from weight

quiz.text: Astronauts on the space station float because…
options: they are too far from Earth
they are in free fall, orbiting the Earth
quiz.explain: Gravity there is still about ninety percent of surface gravity. They are falling around the planet.
quiz.objective: Describe gravity as a force between masses and distinguish mass from weight

quiz.explain: Static has to be beaten first, which is why a box gives suddenly and then slides easily.

quiz.text: A skidding tyre stops a car faster than a rolling one.
quiz.explain: Skidding swaps the larger static grip for smaller kinetic friction. Anti-lock brakes exist to prevent it.

options: towards the centre of the Earth
opposite to the direction of sliding
quiz.explain: It resists the relative motion, whichever way that happens to be.
quiz.objective: Explain what friction is and what it depends on

quiz.text: Where does the energy go when friction slows something down?
quiz.explain: Rub your hands together. The movement energy ends up as heat in the surfaces.
quiz.objective: Explain what friction is and what it depends on

quiz.text: Why does a dry fan bearing make the blade slow down?
options: Friction returns, turning movement into heat and noise
quiz.explain: Without oil the surfaces drag on each other, and the rattle is that friction becoming audible.
quiz.objective: Give cases where friction is wanted and cases where it is a problem

quiz.text: Which of these is a case where friction is wanted?
quiz.explain: Brakes work only because of friction. The other three are places engineers fight to reduce it.
quiz.objective: Give cases where friction is wanted and cases where it is a problem

quiz.text: Gravity is a property of Earth alone.
quiz.explain: Every mass attracts every other mass. Earth is simply the largest one nearby.
quiz.objective: Describe gravity as a force between masses and distinguish mass from weight

quiz.text: Why does a wet road reduce grip?
options: A film of water separates the tyre from the road
quiz.explain: The surfaces stop touching properly, and friction depends on them touching.
quiz.objective: Explain what friction is and what it depends on

quiz.text: The correct term for conditions on the space station is…
quiz.explain: Gravity is nearly as strong as on the ground. The effect of free fall is what makes things float.
quiz.objective: Describe gravity as a force between masses and distinguish mass from weight

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 5 Science, gravity and friction, which the scope then continues into Week 6. Two misconceptions get direct attention because they are the ones that persist: that mass and weight are the same thing, and that astronauts float because gravity has stopped. The static-against-kinetic distinction is taught through the heavy box and then paid off twice, in anti-lock brakes and in a dry fan bearing, so the idea arrives somewhere he can check it himself.
discussion: If gravity is still strong up there, why do they float?
Where in a car do you want friction, and where do you pay to remove it?
Why does a box give suddenly instead of easing into motion?
extension: Push a loaded box across a floor and feel the moment static friction loses.
Spin a fan blade by hand with the plug out, and listen for the bearing.
misconceptions: That weight and mass are the same.
That there is no gravity in orbit.
That friction is always a nuisance.
